subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: The primary purpose of requiring a Bid Bond (Bid Security) in a formal solicitation is to:
options: Guarantee that the project will be completed on time
Ensure that subcontractors will be paid if the prime contractor defaults
Protect the agency against a bidder refusing to execute the contract at their submitted bid price
Fund the agency's procurement department overhead
questions.explain: A bid bond provides a financial guarantee that if the bidder is selected for award, they will honor their bid and sign the contract. If they back out, the bond compensates the agency for the difference in cost to award to the next lowest bidder.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A contractor is halfway through building a new fire station when they file for bankruptcy and walk off the job. Which form of financial security will step in to ensure the project is completed at no additional cost to the agency?
questions.explain: A Performance Bond protects the agency by guaranteeing that the contract will be executed according to the terms and specifications. If the contractor defaults, the surety company is responsible for completing the project.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Under the Miller Act (and state-level Little Miller Acts), which bond is legally mandated for public construction projects exceeding specific thresholds to protect suppliers and subcontractors?
questions.explain: The Miller Act requires a Payment Bond on federal construction contracts over a certain amount (mirrored by state laws) to guarantee that all laborers, material suppliers, and subcontractors will be paid, preventing liens on public property.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: To verify that a vendor maintains adequate workers' compensation and commercial general liability coverage, an agency requires the vendor to submit a:
questions.explain: A Certificate of Insurance (COI) is the standard document issued by an insurance company verifying the existence of insurance policies, coverage amounts, and effective dates for the vendor.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A public agency typically requires vendors to name the agency as an 'Additional Insured' on their General Liability policy. What does this accomplish?
options: It makes the agency responsible for paying the vendor's insurance premiums
It allows the agency's own employees to file claims against the agency
It extends the vendor's insurance coverage to protect the agency from liability arising out of the vendor's operations under the contract
It replaces the need for a performance bond entirely
questions.explain: Naming the agency as an Additional Insured provides direct rights under the vendor's policy, meaning the vendor's insurance will cover and defend the agency if the agency is sued due to the vendor's negligence.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which standard disclosure form requires bidders to swear under oath that their bid was formulated independently, without secret agreements or price-fixing with competitors?
questions.explain: A Non-Collusion Affidavit is a legal document signed by the bidder affirming that they did not participate in any price-fixing, bid-rigging, or anti-competitive behavior while preparing their bid.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which industry type most heavily and consistently requires Bid, Performance, and Payment bonds in public procurement?
questions.explain: Bonds (Bid, Performance, Payment) are heavily utilized and statutorily mandated primarily in the construction and public works industries due to the high financial risk and complexity of such projects.
